_about: B1 도르마크의 심장불 — 카드별 장면 지시. 쓰는 법은 tools/art/PROMPT_GUIDE.md, 검사는 node tools/art/scene_tool.js lint B1.

B1-02.scene: Looking steeply down a stair hacked into a grey cliff: near the top of the frame a small soot-grey mule climbs leftward under two bulging powder sacks roped across its back, a load twice its own bulk, long ears flattened, one ember-rimmed hoof testing the next worn step. The rock face drops away beneath it through drifting ash to the bottom of the frame, where a hair-thin thread of lava glows in the gorge. A dislodged pebble hangs in the air below its hind hoof.
B1-02.light: Flat overcast noon, shadowless and pale; the distant lava thread is the only colour in the whole drop.

B1-03.scene: From behind, low on the stone floor of a powder store: in the right foreground a fat iron bomb is being dragged along by the tarred cord knotted through its lug. The cord — a living fuse — snakes away across the flagstones into the distance, where its sputtering spark-head, tiny and bright, slithers out through the half-open iron door into the night. Every crate edge and broom handle it brushed along the way carries a small new flame.
B1-03.light: Cold blue moonlight falls through the doorway and rims the bomb's curve; the spark and the little flames are the warm points.

B1-05.scene: A tilted, lurching frame catches a knee-high imp of living flame in mid-hop at the lower left, cinder-black body cracked with glowing seams, whip tail of fire lashing as it bounds toward the right and glances back with a cheeky ember-eyed grin. Behind it the bristles of a straw broom sweep in from the left edge, already singed and smoking. Beyond stands a heavy iron-banded door, firmly shut.
B1-05.light: Warm lamplight from a caged lantern on the wall; the imp itself throws a second, flickering glow across the floorboards.

B1-08.scene: First-person view from behind a shield rim: the viewer's own gloved hand presses a rag to the mouth at the bottom edge, and straight ahead, a few paces off, a body of thick gunpowder smoke as tall as a doorway drifts closer over churned ground. A vague grin opens in it, embers wink deep inside like slow eyes, and two long wispy arms unroll toward the cough.
B1-08.light: Night after a cannonade; the only light is the dull orange of the embers buried inside the smoke, glinting on the shield rim.

B1-10.scene: Ground-level view across wet cobblestones beneath a raised iron portcullis: a lean wolf-sized hound with smouldering ember-red fur lies on the right, chin on its soot-black paws, eyes fixed leftward on a pair of muddy boots striding past in the blurred foreground. Its half-open jaws leak a coal-red glow, and each breath lifts a curl of smoke toward the dark gate arch above.
B1-10.light: The only light is the hound's own glowing throat and fur tips, warming the cobbles and the iron teeth of the gate from below.

B1-12.scene: Cat-sized rats with burning silvery-red fur fill the frame from edge to edge, a living tide pouring leftward out of a white-hot crack in the rock at the upper right and over warm rubble. Glowing whiskers, ember eyes and flame-tipped tails repeat like a pattern. One rat near the lower left has stopped to groom, and a tuft of its unburnt fur has caught on an iron comb left on a stone.
B1-12.light: All light pours from the crevice behind them, a blinding core that turns the nearest rats to bright outlines and the far ones to crimson shadow.

B1-13.scene: From the floor of a volcanic shaft, looking straight up: far overhead the round mouth of the crater frames a disc of starry night, and between it and us hundreds of bats spiral upward in a tightening corkscrew, every vein of their leathery wings glowing ember-orange. The sparks shaken from their wings fall back down the shaft toward the viewer like slow burning rain, the nearest ones large and soft.
B1-13.light: Cool blue starlight in the disc above, warm ember light from the wings and falling sparks washing the shaft walls.

B1-14.scene: Through a narrow notch between two rust-red boulders in the foreground we glimpse a wiry soot-dark monkey wedged deep in a crevice on the left, almost entirely hidden: one bright eye, a flattened crest of flame on its head, and a long arm cocked back with a red-hot pebble aimed straight at us. Three earlier stones lie cooling from orange to grey on the gravel just inside the gap.
B1-14.light: Dusk in the rusty hills, wine-dark and dim; the pebble and the pinched crest glow against the shadowed rock.

B1-16.scene: Extreme close-up of two soot-black raccoon paws at work on a workbench: long nimble fingers with small dark claws stretch a fuse cord along a stick cut with plain notches, a small knife already resting on the exact notch. A masked grey muzzle with singed whiskers and the tip of a ringed tail intrude at the top corner. Pushed aside behind the paws lies an abacus with its beads in a hopeless tangle, beside a bundle of charge sticks.
B1-16.light: A single oil lamp just out of frame throws warm amber light across the knuckles and the brass ferrule of the knife.

B1-17.scene: Strict side view, flat as a diagram: on a firing ledge at the left stands a huge tortoise, facing right, its shell of cooled black lava split by glowing seams, a small smoking crater in the middle of its back. From that crater a glowing rock has been lobbed in a high smoke arc across the pale sky. Along the ground runs a row of white range-posts set out for the guns, and the rock is sailing far beyond the last of them toward the right edge.
B1-17.light: Even grey daylight under a high ash haze; the lobbed rock and the shell seams are the only warm notes.

B1-18.scene: A cross-section through the ground: a thin strip along the top shows the plank floor of a powder store with sacks and crates stacked in a row; everything below is dark earth riddled with tunnels and chambers. Dog-sized ants with glossy red-black shells march rightward through them in tight columns, joints and mandibles glowing, one chamber stacked with eggs, another swept perfectly clean directly beneath the stores.
B1-18.light: Underground dark; the ants' own hot joints are the light, a moving chain of small orange points along each tunnel.

B1-21.scene: The frame is tipped along a steep scree slope as a hulking boar hurtles down it from upper right to lower left, smouldering bristles flattened by speed, cinder hooves locked and skidding in a spray of gravel. The red-hot tips of its long tusks draw two glowing streaks through the dark air behind it. Dead ahead in the lower left corner waits a squat stone gatepost.
B1-21.light: Clear cold night with a blue half-moon behind the ridge; the tusk-streaks and sparks under the hooves are the only warm light.

B1-22.scene: Three quarrelling heads crowd the whole frame in close-up: a singed-maned lion roaring on the left, a goat with curled horns butting in from the right, and between and above them a serpent — the beast's own tail — striking down to hiss in both their faces. Each mouth holds a flame at a different stage: a spark, a tongue of fire, a full roaring jet. The cracked hide between the necks glows with heat.
B1-22.light: The three mouth-fires light the heads from within and below, white-hot at the jet, with a thin gold rim from a burning treeline behind.

B1-24.scene: Down beside the baseplate of a stubby mortar, looking up: a stocky wolverine gunner in a scorched leather apron leans back at the lower left with a forepaw clamped over each small round ear, squinting skyward, the tube beside it still breathing smoke. High above, a curved line of smoke climbs over the top of a tall battlement wall toward the right, and at its very tip the shell is a small dark dot against the pale sky.
B1-24.light: Pale overcast afternoon; the last orange of the muzzle flash still glows inside the mortar's mouth.

B1-25.scene: Seen from behind on a rocky rise: the broad warty back of a wagon-sized toad fills the lower centre, its throat sac swollen so huge that it bulges out past both sides of its head, glowing molten through the stretched skin. Far ahead across a darkening valley stands a walled keep; two earlier gobs of lava already burn on its roofs, and a third hangs at the top of its arc above the wall.
B1-25.light: Wine-red dusk; the sac's glow rims the toad's outline from the front and paints the rocks around it orange, with a cool edge of sky-light on its back.

B1-26.scene: Far off on a night mountainside, a man-shaped figure of half-cooled magma — black rock crust, fire leaking from every crack, tall enough to wade through the pines around his knees — stands small in the left third and faces right. Before him rises a colossal spire of dark rock shaped exactly like a single upright finger, knuckle creases and all, many times his height. He holds up his own burning hand beside it to compare.
B1-26.light: Moonless dark; his own cracks are the light, a small fierce glow that reaches only the base of the vast finger.

B1-27.scene: At eye level inside a cluttered workshop: on the right a tall fire spirit — a muscular torso of roaring flame rising from a column of smoke, crowned with sparks — leans toward the whitewashed wall on the left and presses one burning palm flat against it. The wall is already crowded with black star-shaped soot bursts of every size. On the bench between, measuring scoops and open powder jars stand abandoned.
B1-27.light: The spirit's own flame is the lamp of the room, amber on brass tools and deep brown in the rafters.

B1-30.scene: Straight down from high above a hillside of pale dry grass: a bare, blackened track as wide as a road meanders up through it from the bottom edge like a dead river, the grass along its banks withered grey. At the upper right the track ends where an enormous segmented worm arches out of the broken earth and back in, three glowing basalt coils showing, a cart on a nearby lane the size of a seed.
B1-30.light: High thin daylight, almost shadowless; the molten glow between the worm's rings is the single hot colour on the slope.

B1-31.scene: Standing on the bank of a lava river at night: in the left third the head and neck of a great serpent rear out of the molten flow, facing right and upstream, coal-black scales edged in glowing orange, molten fangs dripping. Its long body breaks the surface behind it in two more arcs against the current. On the near bank a bitten tree stump still burns with one small steady flame.
B1-31.light: Deep blue night above, the river's orange glare from below; a cold moon-rim along the serpent's crest.

B1-32.scene: The camera lies on the ground at the rim of a huge footprint filled with glossy black tar, an oily rainbow sheen sliding across it; a long-handled ladle and a half-filled bucket stand at its edge. A line of the same sticky prints leads away up the right side of the frame to their maker, already distant: a slumped, dripping hulk of bitumen shambling off with dull embers sunk in its back.
B1-32.light: A hooded lantern left by the bucket spreads amber light over the tar, which mirrors it like dark brass.

B1-33.scene: Over the craggy shoulder of a walking volcano: its basalt flank and the glowing lip of its open crater fill the right foreground, three lava bombs just flung out and trailing smoke in long arcs to the left. Far below and away, across a dim plain, a walled town the size of a thumbnail sits under the falling stones, a few already burning in its fields. Beneath the cone, one stubby rock leg is planted on a pine wood.
B1-33.light: Violet-brown dusk; the crater's glow lights the flank from within, and a pale rim of last daylight edges the smoke trails.

B1-34.scene: Far across an ash plain, what looked like a mountain ridge is walking: a horned four-legged colossus whose back is a jagged volcanic crest, lava glowing in the cracks of its hide like distant campfires. It crosses the horizon from right to left, as tall as the range behind it. In the lower foreground a tiny cart road with a row of milestones lies in its shadow, already broken by one crater-sized footprint.
B1-34.light: The last red light behind the range turns the beast into a dark mass; its lava seams are the only warm points on the darkening plain.

B1-36.scene: Dead-on and symmetrical: a huge soot-black lion sits enthroned at the centre on a stepped pyramid of stacked iron bombs and brass shell casings, forepaws planted wide, jaws open in a roar straight at us. His mane is a great ruff of fuse cords, every strand lit and spitting sparks like candles on a cake, and a small iron crown rides the top of it. At the foot of the pyramid, tiny soot-furred attendants on both sides crouch with their paws over their ears.
B1-36.light: The ring of mane-sparks is the light, white-hot around his face and falling to deep crimson down the steps of the pyramid.

B1-41.scene: A vast flat ash plain under a night sky, seen from far off: across its whole width runs one thin, faintly smoking line in a slow curve, and at its near end, small in the lower part of the frame, a large snail inches leftward under a shell crusted with grey ash, a molten glow leaking from beneath the rim. Beside the trail lies a single dropped leather glove, its fingertips charred.
B1-41.light: Blue moonlight silvers the ash and the long trail; the warm seam under the shell and a cool glint on its crust mark the snail.

B1-42.scene: Looking down from above onto a wobbling blob of molten rock the size of a cart, black crust plates drifting on its glowing surface like continents around a hollow that suggests a face. Three cannonballs sit half-swallowed in it, slow ripples spreading from each. At its edge lies a sword whose blade droops over the crust like a melted candle, the hilt still cool and dark on the stone floor.
B1-42.light: The slime is its own light, white-yellow at the core and orange at the rim, with a hard glint on the cannonballs' upper curves.

B1-43.scene: A black outline plugs the V-shaped notch of a mountain pass: a squat walking kiln as tall as a gatehouse, seen from behind, brick shoulders, stubby legs and a smoking chimney for a head, all in flat silhouette. The glow of its open furnace mouth pours away from us down the far slope, turning the smoke beyond into an orange fan against which its shape is cut. On the near side the ground lies dark and calm.
B1-43.light: Backlit entirely by its own furnace; a thin orange edge catches the rivets and the chimney smoke, the rest near-black.

EP-B1-1.scene: On a storm-lashed parapet a wiry long-armed monkey with soot-dark fur and a crest of flame stands braced in the left third, bandoliers heavy with round grenades. Its throwing arm repeats in eight overlapping ghost positions like an opening fan, and from each a fizzing grenade has just left: dozens of them hang in a wide rising arc that sweeps across the whole sky to the right, every lit fuse drawing its own bright thread through the slanting rain.
EP-B1-1.light: Indigo storm night with wind-torn cloud; the swarm of fuse-sparks lights the rain and its bared teeth from the right.

EP-B1-2.scene: Over the shoulder of a great bird of fire in a vertical dive: its blazing head and one swept-back wing fill the upper left, feathers burning to ash and rekindling in the slipstream, long flame plumes streaming up out of frame. We look straight down past its beak through a hole punched in the cloud deck to a tiny gun battery on a mountain spur far below, where one lit fuse shows as a single pinpoint.
EP-B1-2.light: Wine-red dusk above the clouds, the volcanic slopes glowing from below through the gap; the bird's own fire lights the torn cloud edges.

EP-B1-3.scene: In strict side view a monstrous cast-iron cannon, long as a street and filling the right two-thirds of the frame, rears its barrel like a raised head toward the left, carriage wheels splayed like forelegs, snapped chains swinging, scaffolding and ladders clinging to its flank like twigs. Its muzzle glows dull red. Far away at the left edge, beyond a driving ash-storm, a volcano smokes, and a tiny winged shape circles its summit.
EP-B1-3.light: Pale storm light sifted through blowing ash, with lightning flickering in the volcano's plume; the heating muzzle is the one warm note.

PN-B1-C1.scene: A tight close-up in the ash of a hearth: a small lizard with wet-looking skin of living flame lies curled along the bottom of the frame, head to the right, one eye half open in mild annoyance. Its tail stands up behind it burning like a lamp wick, and from the top edge the frayed end of a slow-match cord dips down to touch the tail-tip and catch.
PN-B1-C1.light: The lizard's own glow warms the grey ash and the sooty hearth bricks behind; the room beyond is brown dark.

PN-B1-C3.scene: First person, and in the worst place to stand: an ox-sized scorched-black beetle is seen from directly behind, wing-cases toward us, hind legs braced and abdomen hoisted high so that its nozzle points straight into the lens. A cone of boiling, burning spray is already bursting from it, the nearest droplets huge and blurred, while a second charge swells bright inside the abdomen plates.
PN-B1-C3.light: The spray itself is the light, white-yellow at its core and orange at the edges, throwing the beetle's legs into crimson shadow.

PN-B1-E.scene: A still black crater lake fills the frame, and in it hangs the reflection of a jagged ember the size of a boulder — a glowing crystal with a cracked rock rind, floating just above the water, the real thing cropped by the top edge. Each beat of its light sends a perfect ring racing outward across the lake, so the reflection trembles inside five concentric circles. Shore pebbles hover a finger's width above the ground, mist recoiling from every pulse.
PN-B1-E.light: Deep indigo night; the shard's orange-white pulse is the only light, caught on each ring crest and on the underside of the mist.

PN-B1-U1.scene: In flat side view on a dark stone floor: at the left squats a pot-bellied iron brazier on three legs, a flame face peering out between its grate bars toward the right. A line of spilled black powder trails across the floor in front of it, and above that line one stray spark drifts down through the dark. The brazier has shot out a thin tongue of flame, frog-quick, to catch the spark in mid-air.
PN-B1-U1.light: Almost total dark; the coals behind the grate throw barred orange light across the floor and the powder grains.

PN-B1-U2.scene: Glowing threads of molten stone cross the near foreground like the strands of a harp, and through them we see the weaver in the right of the frame: a spider as big as a carriage, obsidian legs and a swollen magma abdomen, walking leftward along its web strung between two colossal curved pillars of rock that rise like ribs. Caught in the nearest strands, a bat and a bird have already cooled to grey stone.
PN-B1-U2.light: A cavern lit from below by a magma glow, violet-brown above; the fresh threads shine orange and dull to grey where they have set.

TK-U-BOMB.scene: A single squat powder keg stands alone in the right of the frame on the floor of an empty trench bay, a plain black barrel shape against a low distant glow. From its bung rises a short fuse, and the spark eating it is the one bright thing in the picture, a thin thread of smoke climbing straight up into the night air.
TK-U-BOMB.light: Deep blue night; a far fire on the horizon outlines the keg, and the fuse-spark touches its top hoop with orange.

UN-B1.scene: Seen from directly above: an old red fox in an artillery captain's scorched coat lies on his back on the flagstones of a gun platform, legs flung wide, muzzle gone grey, ear tips singed, a cracked brass spyglass beside him — and his jaws hang open in a grin. From his outstretched right forepaw a lit fuse runs across the stones in a hissing spiral toward a ring of twelve powder kegs that surrounds him. Long shadows of advancing spearmen reach into the frame from the top edge.
UN-B1.light: The spiralling spark and a toppled lantern light him from one side; everything beyond the kegs is deep night.

UN-B1-7.scene: From deep inside a cannon barrel, looking out through the round mouth of the bore: the dark rifled iron makes a ring around the whole picture, and framed in the bright circle at its centre a tall ash-grey stork leans in toward us, one eye turned to the bore, lowering a shell gripped in its long black beak like tongs. Sunk into the shell's nose is an ember that beats like a heart, black-red and dripping fire. Over its shoulder, down on the plain, yesterday's hits still burn in a dotted line.
UN-B1-7.light: The pulsing ember lights its beak and throat from below, white-hot at its core; a thin gold dawn outlines its neck and folded wings.

UP-B1-12.scene: Framed by the round mouth of a burrow ringed with stones and roots: inside, at the left, one big rat rears upright on its hind legs facing right, silvery-red fur burning steadily, whiskers glowing, ember eyes sharp, a loop of measuring cord worn across its chest like a sash of rank. Behind it the tunnel runs away into the earth, and along one wall neat bundles of charges sit at even intervals, linked by a single cord.
UP-B1-12.light: Its burning fur fills the burrow with amber light, bright on the root tips at the opening and fading to brown down the tunnel.

UP-B1-17.scene: Head-on and perfectly centred: a huge old tortoise faces us squarely, blunt head low between pillar legs, its shell of cooled black lava split by glowing seams and reinforced with scorched brass bands. Where one crater used to be, three smoking vents now rise from its back in a row, and all three are firing at once — three columns of fire and stones leaning together into one plume overhead. The ground under its feet has sunk in a single shallow dish.
UP-B1-17.light: Dusk gloom; the three eruptions light the shell from above and the seams glow from within, wine-red shadow everywhere else.

UP-B1-18.scene: The whole frame is a wall of ants: dog-sized bodies with glossy red-black shells locked together shoulder to shoulder and stacked row on row like fitted masonry, heads tucked, mandibles meshed, facing us. Every joint glows hot. Where blows have landed, three patches of shell shine yellow-white, and in front of one a snapped spear and a bent arrow are still tumbling away.
UP-B1-18.light: Warm amber glow rises from the joints across the whole wall; the struck patches are the brightest points.

UP-B1-24.scene: Its back is to us: the same stocky wolverine gunner in a scorched apron stands upright on an ammunition crate in the left of the frame, one foreleg stretched out with a single claw raised to sight along it, small round ears and thick ruff black against the sky. Beyond it the night is ruled with glowing shell trails — its own a single clean high arc, and beneath it a spray of lower, wobblier arcs from the mortar pits down the line, where small crews are cranking their tubes to match.
UP-B1-24.light: Deep blue night; the arcs glow orange like long-exposure trails and rim its shoulders and ruff with warm light.

CS-B1.scene: The moment after: in the centre of a ring of white ash lies a great spring-jawed trap, sprung and ruined — iron teeth warped, its coiled spring unwound and still glowing, the trigger plate sagging, the charred stub of a thrown torch clamped in its jaws. Soot fans outward across the ground in a starburst, broken only by two clean shapes where two shields stood, both now lying face down.
CS-B1.light: Grey smoky daylight; the cooling spring is the single orange thing left, with a thin bright edge along the warped teeth.

HB1-1.scene: Five identical ammunition crates stand in a neat row across a dark field, evenly spaced like pieces laid out for a game, seen straight on. Four sit untouched and cold. The second from the right is wholly ablaze, lid lifting, flames roaring upward and throwing the long shadows of the others across the grass. In the foreground lie three small hooded lanterns; two have tipped over and gone dark.
HB1-1.light: Midnight, moonless and blue-black; the one burning crate is the whole light of the scene.

MB-01.scene: Under a low grey sky the air is full of iron: hundreds of dark musket-ball-sized shot fill the frame from edge to edge, each drawn out into a short slanting streak, falling to the lower left like a rain squall seen from the side. Where the first of them land, a ploughed field jumps in dozens of small spurts of mud, and a lone wicker shield planted in the furrows is already coming apart.
MB-01.light: Dull daylight; each ball carries a faint orange heat-glint on its leading side, the only colour in the grey.

MB-04.scene: A thin fuse cord lies across cracked dry ground in a long S-curve from the lower left corner to the upper right, where it vanishes between the planted boots of a shield line seen only from the knees down. Halfway along, a hissing spark eats the cord and throws up a low trail of smoke — charred black line behind it, clean pale cord still ahead.
MB-04.light: Deep night; the travelling spark is the single light, picking out pebbles, boot-toes and the lower rims of the shields.

MB-05.scene: Extremely close on a burlap sack splitting open in mid-air at the top of the frame: the coarse weave chars and tears, and hundreds of small live coals spill out of the rip and tumble down and to the right, the nearest ones sharp enough to show their cracked, pulsing surfaces and the hair of smoke each one trails. Far below, out of focus, lie the pale ridges of sleeping tents.
MB-05.light: Black night; the coals light themselves and the torn edge of the sack, everything else lost in dark.

MC-02.scene: Two long bayonets lie side by side across a wet grey whetstone in the right of the frame, points to the right, freshly honed. Their polished flats work as narrow mirrors: in them runs the reflection of a pale evening sky and, along the bottom, a row of tiny orange match-lights waiting in the dusk. A bright hairline of light travels the full length of each edge, and beads of water stand on the stone.
MC-02.light: Soft grey last light from above; the reflected match-lights are the one warm colour, doubled along both blades.

MC-16.scene: Straight overhead above a dark field at the instant a barrage lands: a dozen small shell-bursts blossom all across the frame like white-hot flowers, each with its own ring of flung earth, and at the bottom edge two far larger bursts open side by side, their shock rings overlapping. Between the blasts the ground shows the faint grid of trampled paths and a few abandoned shields, tiny as coins.
MC-16.light: Night; every burst is its own light, yellow-white at the heart and crimson where the smoke begins.

NB1-1.scene: Seen exactly side-on: at the left a thick iron-bound shield stands planted in the earth with a clean round hole punched through its centre, splinters and rivets still flying out of the back. To the right of it the cannonball that made the hole — banded in layers of dark iron, glowing dull at the seams — is still going, skipping along the ground in a long shallow furrow marked by a row of dust puffs that runs to the right edge.
NB1-1.light: Low amber evening light from the left turns the dust puffs to brass and throws the shield's long shadow along the furrow.

PS-B1-1.scene: A huge two-handed war axe is caught at the top of its swing in the right of the frame, raised against the night sky, and it is half one thing and half another: the lower haft and the two gauntlets gripping it are still whole and dark, while from the middle upward the weapon is turning into a burst of fire, the head splitting along glowing cracks and its fragments already flying. Loose grains of black powder trickle from the haft.
PS-B1-1.light: Deep blue night; the bursting head is the light, orange-white, with a cold moon-rim on the steel of the gauntlets.

PS-B1-2.scene: Two fuse cords hang straight down the centre of the frame side by side, taut and vertical from top to bottom in the dark. On each, at exactly the same height, a spark is climbing: below the sparks the cords are already grey curls of ash drifting away, above them still clean and pale. At the very top edge the round iron bellies of two bombs just enter the picture.
PS-B1-2.light: Pitch dark all round; the two sparks are the only light, each ringed by a small orange halo of lit smoke.

RB1-1.scene: A cross-section of a trench line under a dusk sky: the cut earth shows three firing bays dug side by side in the lower half of the frame, and in each bay, where a defender should stand, sits a powder keg with its fuse lit. A single dented helmet rests on the parapet. Above the grass line, at the top edge, the tips of spears and the toes of many boots are arriving.
RB1-1.light: Wine-red dusk above ground; down in the bays the three fuse-sparks light the kegs and the raw earth walls from below.

SB1-01.scene: From inside a rolling bank of thick yellow-grey powder smoke: vague shapes of spears and helmets dissolve a few paces away, and three wavering orange glows — small fires clinging to unseen shields — are the only fixed points in the murk. At the bottom edge a cracked clay smoke-pot still spins on the trampled ground, pouring out fresh smoke.
SB1-01.light: Flat, choked daylight filtered through the smoke; the three small fires hang in it like lanterns in fog.

SB1-03.scene: Standing at the near end of a long ditch and looking straight down its length: a channel of dark glistening oil runs away from us to the vanishing point, and a wall of flame is racing along it into the distance, already standing man-high where it has passed. On the left the fire lights an empty parapet of sandbags; on the right, open ground where the tip of a dropped sword lies burning.
SB1-03.light: Night; the fire-wall is the light, yellow-white at its base and deep red in the smoke rolling off its top.

SB1-05.scene: Across a black plain, very far away: a long column on the march shows only as a row of small clinging fires strung along the lower part of the frame like beads — and at this instant every one of them bursts at once into an identical round fireball. High in the upper right a single red signal rocket hangs at the top of its climb, the cue they all answered.
SB1-05.light: Moonless night; the row of bursts and the lone rocket are the only lights, each with a thin gold rim of lit smoke.

SB1-06.scene: Inside the dark of a casemate, the view is framed by a wide low gun-slit: the smoking muzzle of a concealed cannon juts into the left foreground, and out in the daylight beyond, a shield line advances toward us across open ground. A shot has just landed behind it, among the rear rank — a burst of earth and smoke — and the helmets of the front rank are only now turning to look back.
SB1-06.light: Warm slow-match glow on the cannon's brass inside the dark vault; flat daylight outside, a thin bright edge on the slit's stone.

SB1-08.scene: The exact instant a stone powder house lets go, seen from close by: its slate roof lifts off whole on a dome of white fire, the walls bulge outward stone by stone with light blazing through every opening joint, and the iron-banded door hangs in mid-air a pace in front of its frame. Barrel staves and hoops are already spinning out of the glare toward every edge of the picture.
SB1-08.light: The blast is the light: a blinding yellow-white core, orange through the gaps in the stonework, crimson shadow beyond, with gold glints on the flying hoops.

SB1-09.scene: One landscape, half changed: the left half of the frame is still a quiet meadow with a lane, a fence and a line of poplars; the right half is a grey moonscape of overlapping craters, splintered stumps and standing smoke. Between the two runs a wall of earth caught in mid-air, a whole line of shells bursting at once as the bombardment walks leftward across the land.
SB1-09.light: Overcast and ash-pale; the row of bursts at the seam carries the only orange, lighting the smoke from inside.

US-B1-1.scene: A single pillar of fire and smoke stands in the centre of the frame, rising from a dropped powder sack on a night road straight up through the cloud layer, where it has punched a ring-shaped hole and the clouds are rolling back from it. At its foot the blast spreads sideways in a low expanding ring that is lifting a whole line of shields, carts and tent-poles off the ground. The pillar's upper half mushrooms above the clouds.
US-B1-1.light: Deep indigo night; the pillar lights the undersides of the retreating clouds orange and throws long shadows outward along the road.

US-B1-2.scene: A side view of one shell's whole flight across a stormy dusk sky, from right to left: its glowing trail climbs out of the lower right, and high in the middle of the frame the shell has burst once — a wide ring of fire and sparks pushing the storm clouds apart. Out of that ring a white-hot core has kept going, and at the lower left it strikes the ridge and bursts a second time, larger, the two blasts joined by one curving thread of light.
US-B1-2.light: Violet-brown storm dusk with rain curtains on the horizon; both bursts light the cloud bellies from inside, the land below in wine-dark shadow.

IB1-1.scene: A heavy walnut musket stock lies where it was last swung, in the right of the frame on trampled ground: its barrel bent, the brass butt-plate cracked and smeared with mud, resting across an iron helm with a deep fresh dent in its crown. Splinters of the stock are scattered around, and the gun's slow-match, still looped through the lock, smoulders with one small red coal.
IB1-1.light: Night after the fighting; the match-coal is the single light, a small orange glow on wood grain, brass and the dented steel.

IB1-2.scene: A broad leather belt hangs from an iron peg in the middle of the frame, lit from behind so that its load reads in outline: a row of small corked powder flasks in stitched loops, each with a short fuse standing up like a stalk. One loop near the buckle hangs empty. The leather is scorched along its lower edge, and a tinderbox dangles from it on a thong.
IB1-2.light: A forge glow behind the belt rims every flask in amber; the front is soft brown shadow with a glint on the buckle.

IB1-3.scene: Laid out and seen from straight above on a square of grey oilcloth: a short, heavy blunderbuss lies on the diagonal with its trumpet-flared muzzle toward the upper right. Around it, neatly arranged, are its ramrod, a powder horn, a coil of slow-match with one end faintly smouldering, and a leather pouch that has spilled its mixed shot — iron balls, bent nails and pebbles — across the cloth.
IB1-3.light: Flat pale daylight from a window out of frame; the smouldering match-end is the one orange point.

IB1-4.scene: A brass spyglass, dented and wrapped in scorched leather, rests fully extended on a sandbag at the lip of a gun emplacement, set in the left of the frame and pointing away into the dusk. Its wide front lens, turned three-quarters toward us, holds a tiny, sharp, upside-down image of a distant fortified ridge, with one bright point of light exactly where the wall is cracked.
IB1-4.light: Low orange dusk glints along the brass tube; the little image inside the lens is the brightest thing in the picture.

IB1-5.scene: So close that the breech of a hand-cannon fills the frame: thick heat-blued iron clamped by four bolts around a small round window of smoky crystal, and behind the crystal a shard of living fire pulses in its chamber, pressing light out through every hairline gap. The brass sighting rail above it is worn bright by a thumb, and the wood of the stock below is charred in a clean arc.
IB1-5.light: Cold blue night light on the iron; the shard's orange glow leaks through the crystal and edges each bolt head in gold.

PI-B1.scene: A fist-sized clot of living fire lies where it was set down on a slab of black basalt in the lower part of the frame, and it has melted itself a shallow glassy bowl in the rock. Rain is falling hard, and every drop turns to steam before it lands, so a white column climbs from the fire into the storm. A pair of long iron tongs lies beside it, the tips drooping and half melted.
PI-B1.light: Storm dark; the clot is the light, blinding yellow-white at its heart, turning the steam column orange and the wet rock crimson.

IR-B1.scene: At the right of the frame a single hand in a scorched leather glove, cropped at the wrist, holds a long matchlock musket upright by its fore-end, muzzle to the sky, a last thread of smoke leaving the barrel and the match cord glowing in its lock. The walnut stock is turned toward us: row under row of knife-cut notches cover it from the lock down to the brass butt-plate, the newest still pale. Far off at the left a long row of clay pots stands on a lava-stone wall, each holed through its exact middle.
IR-B1.light: Sooty amber dusk on a firing range; the glowing match cord and a low furnace-orange horizon warm the brass fittings and catch the edge of every notch.

NB1-3.scene: Lying on the floor of a narrow mountain pass at night and looking straight up: the strip of sky between two black rock walls has become a river of wind made visible, long streamers of sparks and thin flame all racing leftward across the upper frame. Tall pennons on spear shafts lean in from below, snapping the same way; the foremost is ablaze along its whole length, those behind it only fringed with fire. Loose embers sift down toward the lens like slow snow and settle as tiny flames on helmet crests and spear tips.
NB1-3.light: Deep night in the pass; the wind's own orange streamers overhead and the pinpoint embers settling on black iron are the only light.

PN-B1-R.scene: The camera sits on the flagstones of a gun bastion beside a carriage wheel, deep in pale drifting powder smoke. Along the wall three gun crews in leather aprons work with blurred hands: a rammer driven home, a charge passed along, a linstock already swinging down. High in the right of the frame, seen from below and behind, a hawk with dark ember-edged wings banks away from us into the smoke, its thin fire trail closing one full circle above the battery. Sparks shed from its feathers drift down, and every slow-match they touch flares.
PN-B1-R.light: Bone-white smoke flattens the daylight to pale grey; the hawk's circling fire trail and the flaring matches are the only orange.

RS-B1-1.scene: From a cliff-top battery we look down on a valley floor turned to a level sea of flame, shore to shore between black cliffs. At its centre the newest shell has just landed, and from that point ring-waves of fire roll outward one inside another, as ripples spread on a pond; a dozen smaller rings from other hits overlap them across the whole surface. A wrecked siege tower leans half-sunk in the burning, and more shells are still arcing down through the smoke. At the frame's lower edge lies a heap of emptied powder kegs.
RS-B1-1.light: Violet-brown dusk under a lid of smoke; the fire sea lights the cliffs wine-red from below, and each ring crest burns orange-white.

RS-B1-2.scene: First person, looking straight down at our own two boots on a steep mountain path paved with flat lava stones. Under the left boot, in the left of the frame, one stone like all the others has sunk a finger's depth, and a hair-thin seam of orange light has sprung up around it and is racing along the cracks toward a second stone one stride ahead. Smoke curls up between the bootlaces and the first grit is already lifting toward the lens. Beside the sunken stone, easy to miss, three pebbles sit in a deliberate row.
RS-B1-2.light: Late amber light on soot-brown rock; the seam of fire under the boot is the brightest thing, glinting on brass eyelets and hobnails.

RS-B1-3.scene: One enormous two-handed sword stands raised, high at the right of the frame, above a dark rank of helmets and ordinary spears. From three shell-bursts fading in the sky behind, thousands of freed embers stream across the whole picture in long bending lines that all curve toward that single blade and crowd onto it. Its upper half is already sheathed in them and glowing yellow-white, sparks dripping from the cross-guard onto the gauntlets that hold it. The spears and short blades around it carry only an ember or two apiece.
RS-B1-3.light: Black smoke-filled sky; the ember-crusted blade is the light source, blinding yellow-white along its edge and sinking to crimson on the helmets beneath.

SP-B1.scene: Many miles away across a dark ash plain: the tallest peak of a volcanic range, at the left of the frame, is a seated figure of black basalt — knees drawn up like two spurs, shoulders in cloud, a furnace-bright fire showing through the cracks of its ribs. Its head turns to the right and it breathes out: the breath leaves as a level rank of fire-bolts, side by side like one battery's salvo, and along the skyline ahead every crater has lit in answer, one tall flame in each. At its ankle a fortress's chimneys stand small as stubble.
SP-B1.light: Blue-black night with a low moon behind thin smoke; the rib-glow, the salvo and the lit craters string one line of orange across the indigo.

SR-B1.scene: Under the mountain, a vault arched by the ribs of something colossal: ash-pale bone, each rib thick as a tower, curving into the dark. One rib ends in a sawn stump high on the wall. Beneath that gap, in the right of the frame, stands what was made from it — a brazier taller than a doorway, carved from one length of the same pale bone and banded with black iron, full of low orange fire. On the step below, one offering candle burns, and the brazier's flames have doubled, leaning down over the rim toward it.
SR-B1.light: Muted ash-pale gloom under the bone vault; the brazier is the single orange source, throwing long rib shadows up the walls.
